arxiv-1606-00569.title: Fixed Point Algebras for Easy Quantum Groups
arxiv-1606-00569.creator: Olivier GABRIEL † and Moritz WEBER ‡
arxiv-1606-00569.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Olivier GABRIEL † and Moritz WEBER ‡. Compact matrix quantum groups act naturally on Cuntz algebras. The first author isolated certain conditions under which the fixed point algebras under this action are Kirchberg algebras. Hence they are completely determined by their K K -groups. Building on prior work by the second author, we prove that free easy quantum groups satisfy these conditions and we compute the K K -groups of their fixed point algebras in a general form.

arxiv-2304-12069.title: Occlusion Robust 3D Human Pose Estimation with StridedPoseGraphFormer and Data Augmentation Code is available at https://github.com/baniks/StridedPoseGraphFormer .
arxiv-2304-12069.creator: Soubarna Banik 1 , Patricia Gschoßmann 1 , Alejandro Mendoza García 2 , Alois Knoll 1
arxiv-2304-12069.description: Abstract Occlusion is an omnipresent challenge in 3D human pose estimation (HPE). In spite of the large amount of research dedicated to 3D HPE, only a limited number of studies address the problem of occlusion explicitly. To fill this gap, we propose to combine exploitation of spatio-temporal features with synthetic occlusion augmentation during training to deal with occlusion.

arxiv-2401-09575.title: Zero Trust Implementation in the Emerging Technologies Era: Survey Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2401-09575.creator: Abraham Itzhak Weinberg, Kelly Cohen
arxiv-2401-09575.description: Abstract This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the shift from the traditional perimeter model of security to the Zero Trust (ZT) framework, emphasizing the key points in the transition and the practical application of ZT. It outlines the differences between ZT policies and legacy security policies, along with the significant events that have impacted the evolution of ZT.

arxiv-2401-12980.title: Identifying Risk Patterns in Brazilian Police Reports Preceding Femicides: A Long Short Term Memory (LSTM) Based Analysis
arxiv-2401-12980.creator: Vinicius Lima, Jacque Almeida de Oliveira
arxiv-2401-12980.description: Abstract Femicide refers to the killing of a female victim, often perpetrated by an intimate partner or family member, and is also associated with gender-based violence. Studies have shown that there is a pattern of escalating violence leading up to these killings, highlighting the potential for prevention if the level of danger to the victim can be assessed.

arxiv-2407-14588.title: Forecasts and Statistical Insights for Line Intensity Mapping Cross-Correlations: A Case Study with 21cm × \times [CII]
arxiv-2407-14588.creator: Hannah Fronenberg, Adrian Liu
arxiv-2407-14588.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Hannah Fronenberg, Adrian Liu. Intensity mapping—the large-scale mapping of selected spectral lines without resolving individual sources—is quickly emerging as an efficient way to conduct large cosmological surveys. Multiple surveys covering a variety of lines (such as the hydrogen 21 cm hyperfine line, CO rotational lines, and [CII] fine structure lines, among others) are either observing or will soon be online, promising a panchromatic view of our Universe over a broad redshift range.

arxiv-2410-15051.title: Automatic identification of diagnosis from hospital discharge letters via weakly supervised Natural Language Processing
arxiv-2410-15051.creator: Vittorio Torri, Elisa Barbieri, Anna Cantarutti, Carlo Giaquinto, Francesca Ieva
arxiv-2410-15051.description: Abstract Identifying patient diagnoses from hospital discharge letters is essential for large-scale cohort selection and epidemiological research, but traditional supervised approaches require extensive manual annotation, which is often impractical for large textual datasets. We present a weakly supervised Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline for classifying Italian discharge letters without document-level manual annotation.

arxiv-2411-04171.title: Fractionally Quantized Electric Polarization and Discrete Shift of Crystalline Fractional Chern Insulators
arxiv-2411-04171.creator: Yuxuan Zhang and Maissam Barkeshli
arxiv-2411-04171.description: Abstract Fractional Chern insulators (FCI) with crystalline symmetry possess topological invariants that fundamentally have no analog in continuum fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states. Here we demonstrate through numerical calculations on model wave functions that FCIs possess a fractionally quantized electric polarization, P → o \vec{{P}}_{\text{o}} , where o is a high symmetry point.

arxiv-2502-01713.title: Auditing a Dutch Public Sector Risk Profiling Algorithm Using an Unsupervised Bias Detection Tool
arxiv-2502-01713.creator: Floris Holstege, Mackenzie Jorgensen, Kirtan Padh, Jurriaan Parie, Krsto Proroković, Joel Persson, Lukas Snoek
arxiv-2502-01713.description: Abstract Algorithms are increasingly used to automate or aid human decisions, yet recent research shows that these algorithms may exhibit bias across legally protected demographic groups. However, data on these groups may be unavailable to organizations or external auditors due to privacy legislation.

pmc-10542608.description: E. coli is one of the most widely used organisms for understanding the principles of cellular and molecular genetics. However, we are yet to understand the origin of several experimental observations related to the regulation of gene expression in E. coli.

pmc-10738430.title: CHANGES IN MULTIMORBIDITY AMONG HOSPITALIZED ADULTS IN THE US
pmc-10738430.creator: Lauren Picken, Yue Zhang, Christine Loyd
pmc-10738430.description: Having multiple chronic health conditions, or multimorbidity, is common among adult inpatients and is associated with risk of death, disability, and reduced quality of life. This investigation examines prevalence trends of multimorbidity over time among inpatients based on age, sex, and race and assesses hospitalization rates for individual diseases over time.

pmc-12635663.title: Effectiveness of non-invasive interventions for internet gaming disorder: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12635663.creator: Haewon Byeon
pmc-12635663.description: BACKGROUNDInternet gaming disorder (IGD) is a growing concern among adolescents and adults, necessitating effective treatment strategies beyond pharmacological interventions.AIMTo evaluated the effectiveness of non-invasive interventions for treating IGD among adolescents and adults.METHODSA total of 11 randomized controlled trials published between 2020 and 2025 were included in this meta-analysis, encompassing 1208 participants from diverse geographic and cultural contexts.

pmc-12789083.title: Usable time estimation and suitable battery selection for electric tractor considering agricultural operational load
pmc-12789083.creator: Md. Abu Ayub Siddique, Cheol-Woo Yang, Nyunki Chung, Seung-Min Baek, Seung-Yun Baek, Hyeon-Ho Jeon, Yeon-Soo Kim, Wan-Soo Kim, Yong-Joo Kim
pmc-12789083.description: This study estimates battery usable time and discharge rates, and selects a suitable battery for a single-motor electric tractor using dynamometer tests and rotary tillage at L-slow, L-fast, and M-slow gear stages. The dynamometer results were validated for rotary tillage to determine a suitable battery for full-day (8 h) operations.

pmc-13240419.title: Occurrence of Antimicrobial‐Resistant Listeria monocytogenes and Listeria spp. Recovered From Cattle Farms and the Factors Associated With Their Distribution in Mpumalanga and North West Provinces in South Africa
pmc-13240419.creator: K C Moabelo, N C Mtshali, R Moerane, N Gcebe, Y B Ngoshe, A A Adesiyun, Lipi Buch
pmc-13240419.description: Two cross‐sectional studies determined the prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Listeria monocytogenes and Listeria spp. isolated from cattle farms in Mpumalanga and North West provinces in South Africa. A total of 100 isolates comprise 12 and 44 of L. monocytogenes and Listeria spp., respectively, from Mpumalanga province and 3 and 41 from North West province.

pmc-13283201.title: Retesting reverse-reward performance in capuchin monkeys (Sapajus apella) after 16 years: evidence of aging-related decline
pmc-13283201.creator: Yui Sugimoto, James R Anderson, Hika Kuroshima
pmc-13283201.description: In reverse-reward contingency tasks, the subject chooses between two potential rewards differing in value. To receive the higher-value reward, the subject must reach toward the lower-value reward; any reach toward the higher-value reward results in receiving the lower-value reward. In studies on animals, the rewards are usually food items differing in quantity or quality.

pmc-13414148.title: Do archery athletes’ hand dexterity, strength, and cognition exceed those of age-matched athletes and non-athletes? A cross-sectional study
pmc-13414148.creator: Xinpeng Gao, Fuxin Hong, Jinlong Hou, Yanan Gao, Qianqian Han, Ming Li
pmc-13414148.description: PurposeSport-specific training may reshape athletes’ executive function and manual fine-motor control in a discipline-specific manner, affecting the efficiency of sensorimotor-cognitive coupling. Open-skill and closed-skill sports differ in environmental uncertainty and movement stability demands, but direct comparisons of hand dexterity, inhibitory control, and their interrelations across these sport types are limited.

pmc-13542449.title: Short-term milk production responses differ when balancing dietary 18-carbon fatty acids using high-oleic soybeans or a commercially available stearic acid-enriched supplement
pmc-13542449.creator: Brooke A. Seelenbinder, Jair E. Parales-Girón, Alycia M. Bales, Adam L. Lock
pmc-13542449.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Graphical AbstractSummary: This study assessed the effects of balancing 18-carbon fatty acids in mid-lactation dairy cows by using either high-oleic soybeans (HOS) or a supplement enriched with stearic acid (SAT), while keeping the intake of 16-carbon fatty acids similar. In a 2-treatment crossover design, HOS increased the yields of milk and milk components as well as feed efficiency compared with SAT, despite reducing dry matter intake (DMI).

pmc-13657679.title: Development of CRISPR/Cas13-based analytical tools to study RNA–protein interactions
pmc-13657679.creator: Keita Yamamoto, Shiori Shikata, Yangying Hao, Takuya Tomita, Rina Kanai, Els Verhoeyen, Yasushi Saeki, Susumu Goyama
pmc-13657679.description: RNA–protein interactions (RPIs) are as important as protein–protein interactions (PPIs) for the formation of membraneless organelles (MLOs) and play vital roles in diverse biological processes. Despite remarkable advances in PPI analysis technologies, the development of tools for RPI analysis has lagged behind. To address this challenge, we integrated three established PPI technologies—bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), NanoBiT, and split-TurboID—with RNA-targeting CRISPR/dCas13.
